_licence.source: Runcible curated keyboard facts, written for this Book
_licence.note: Every row states where a key sits on a piano keyboard. A key's position is a fact of the instrument, not a passage of anybody's prose, which is why this file is authored rather than declared: no corpus publishes it and there is nothing here to attribute. musictheory.net and Hoffman Academy teach the same facts and neither grants a licence, so nothing of theirs is copied and both stay links in the chapters.

title: The twelve keys of one octave, by where they sit

fields.name: what the key is called. One string in both languages, and the reason is not that a name has no Spanish: it does, and chapter 1 prints it. It is that books/piano/exercises/staff.js reads this field raw to build the expected answer, the option labels and the label pool of the drawn drill, so an { en, es } here would put [object Object] on four buttons. Making it bilingual is a change to that module and to this file together.
fields.position: where the key is, said without naming another key. The prompt of the choice drill, read through the shell's own field reader, so it is { en, es } and a Spanish reader is asked in Spanish.
fields.pc: 0 for C up to 11 for B, so a drawn keyboard needs no lookup table.
fields.note: one line the drill can show after the answer. One string in both languages, for the same reason as name: the drawn drill passes it through untouched.
fields._bilingual: An item field named by prompt, answer, left, right, speak, expect or sequence resolves to the reader's language through js/exercises/items.js. A field a Book module reads for itself does not, unless that module resolves it, so the two halves of this file are split on exactly that line.

white.name: C

position.en: the white key just to the left of a pair of black keys
position.es: la tecla blanca justo a la izquierda de un par de teclas negras

white.note: C is the anchor. Find the pair of black keys anywhere on the instrument and C is immediately left of it.

white.name: D

position.en: the white key between the two black keys of a pair
position.es: la tecla blanca entre las dos teclas negras de un par

white.note: D sits inside the pair, so it is the one white key with a black key on each side and nothing but the pair around it.

white.name: E

position.en: the white key just to the right of a pair of black keys
position.es: la tecla blanca justo a la derecha de un par de teclas negras

white.note: E closes the pair. C left, D inside, E right.

white.name: F

position.en: the white key just to the left of a group of three black keys
position.es: la tecla blanca justo a la izquierda de un grupo de tres teclas negras

white.note: F opens the group of three the way C opens the pair.

white.name: G

position.en: the white key between the first and second black keys of a group of three
position.es: la tecla blanca entre la primera y la segunda tecla negra de un grupo de tres

white.note: G and A are the two white keys buried inside the group of three.

white.name: A

position.en: the white key between the second and third black keys of a group of three
position.es: la tecla blanca entre la segunda y la tercera tecla negra de un grupo de tres

white.note: A is the second of the two white keys inside the group of three.

white.name: B

position.en: the white key just to the right of a group of three black keys
position.es: la tecla blanca justo a la derecha de un grupo de tres teclas negras

white.note: B closes the group of three, and the next white key to the right is C again.

black.name: C sharp or D flat

position.en: the lower of the two black keys in a pair
position.es: la más grave de las dos teclas negras de un par

black.note: One key, two names. It is C sharp when it is a raised C and D flat when it is a lowered D, and which one is printed depends on the key the music is in.

black.name: D sharp or E flat

position.en: the upper of the two black keys in a pair
position.es: la más aguda de las dos teclas negras de un par

black.note: E flat is the name you meet first, because it belongs to the flat keys a beginner plays in.

black.name: F sharp or G flat

position.en: the lowest of the three black keys in a group
position.es: la más grave de las tres teclas negras de un grupo

black.note: F sharp is the single sharp of G major, which is why it is the first black key most players learn by name.

black.name: G sharp or A flat

position.en: the middle of the three black keys in a group
position.es: la del medio de las tres teclas negras de un grupo

black.note: The middle key of the three, and the only black key with a black key on both sides.

black.name: A sharp or B flat

position.en: the highest of the three black keys in a group
position.es: la más aguda de las tres teclas negras de un grupo

black.note: B flat is the single flat of F major, and it is spelled B flat far more often than A sharp.
